The invention relates to an electronic system and a corresponding method for controlling digital content associated with artworks so as to prevent its unauthorised distribution.

The electronic system (10) includes at least one file-import unit (11) for receiving files containing artwork-related digital content, operatively linked to at least one display unit (12) configured to present that content. outputs.L3:
The invention provides an electronic system and method for managing digital artwork content while preventing unauthorized or uncontrolled distribution. The system includes a file-importing unit connected to at least one digital-content display unit. The file-importing unit is configured to encrypt and decrypt artwork files using a unique cryptographic key associated with the display unit or with one of its electronic components.

In operation, the method obtains a unique identification code from the display unit or a designated component within it. This identification code is then used to generate an encryption key specific to that device. When a digital artwork file is imported, the file-importing unit encrypts the file using the generated key and stores the encrypted file in secure storage. Because the encryption key is tied to the intended display unit, the artwork can be decrypted and displayed only by, or in connection with, the authorized device. This device-specific protection helps preserve control over the digital artwork and limits unauthorized copying, transfer, or use.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a system and method for controlling the import, storage, and display of digital artwork. Conventional digital image files can often be copied, transferred, or distributed without authorization once they have been downloaded or delivered to a user. The invention reduces this risk by binding each imported artwork file to a designated display unit.

When a digital artwork file is received, an import system obtains identification information associated with the intended display unit or with one or more electronic components installed in that unit. The identification information may include, for example, a device identifier, processor identifier, memory identifier, cryptographic-module identifier, or another value that is unique or sufficiently specific to the hardware. The system uses this information, either directly or through a cryptographic derivation process, to generate a unique encryption key.

Before the artwork is placed in persistent storage, the import system encrypts the file using the derived key. The stored version is therefore hardware-bound and cannot ordinarily be opened or rendered by an unrelated computer, display, or storage device. When the authorized display unit is instructed to present the artwork, it obtains the required hardware information, reconstructs or accesses the corresponding key, decrypts the file within a controlled environment, and supplies the resulting image data to the display. Decrypted content may be retained only temporarily and may be protected from access by other applications or users.

If the encrypted file is copied from the authorized unit, the receiving device will not possess the hardware characteristics or secure key material required to decrypt it. Likewise, replacing a protected electronic component may cause validation to fail unless the new component is registered or the artwork is securely re-encrypted for the modified unit. Optional authentication, integrity checking, access logging, and tamper-detection mechanisms may be used to strengthen the system further.

By encrypting digital artwork before storage and tying decryption to specific display hardware, the invention limits the usefulness of unauthorized copies. It thereby provides artists, galleries, distributors, and owners with improved control over access to and dissemination of digital works while still allowing those works to be displayed on approved equipment.
outputs.L5:
## The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest and most frequently used words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a specific person, place, object, or idea. When we say “the book,” we refer not to any book, but to one that the listener already knows or can recognize.

Despite its simplicity, “the” plays an important role in communication. It creates clarity, establishes shared understanding, and gives ordinary nouns a sense of importance. There is a difference between “a solution” and “the solution,” just as there is a difference between “a moment” and “the moment.”

This tiny word shows how language can shape meaning with remarkable precision. Often unnoticed, “the” quietly connects speakers, listeners, and the world they are describing.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for an electronic system and method that securely manages digital artwork files by encrypting them with a unique key derived from hardware identification codes of the display device.
counterfactuals.output: An electronic system and method are provided for securely managing digital artwork files associated with a display device. The system obtains one or more hardware identification codes from the display device and derives a device-specific cryptographic key using a key-derivation function. A digital artwork file is encrypted with the device-specific cryptographic key and stored locally or remotely together with access-control metadata. In response to a request to display the digital artwork, the system authenticates the display device, regenerates or retrieves the device-specific cryptographic key, decrypts the artwork file, and provides the decrypted content to a protected rendering process. The decrypted artwork may be maintained only in volatile memory and removed after rendering or upon detection of an unauthorized condition. Because decryption is bound to hardware identification codes of an authorized display device, copying the encrypted artwork file to another device does not permit usable access, thereby reducing unauthorized reproduction, transfer, or display of the digital artwork.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a European-style patent summary describing an art-content importing unit, a display unit, encryption/decryption means, and a workflow for importing, encrypting, and storing digital artwork to prevent unauthorized diffusion.
counterfactuals.output:
**Title: System and Method for Secure Importation, Display and Storage of Digital Artwork**

The invention relates to a system for controlling the diffusion of digital artwork. The system comprises an art-content importing unit configured to receive digital artwork from an external source, a display unit configured to render the digital artwork, encryption and decryption means, and a secure storage unit. The importing unit obtains artwork data and associated identification and/or usage-control information and transfers the artwork data to the encryption means through a controlled data path. The encryption means encrypts the artwork data using a cryptographic key associated with an authorised device, user or access policy. The resulting encrypted artwork is stored in the secure storage unit, while an unencrypted copy is deleted from, or prevented from being persistently retained in, an import buffer.

Upon receipt of an authorised display request, the decryption means verifies access credentials and decrypts at least a portion of the stored artwork for presentation by the display unit. Decrypted data is supplied to the display unit in volatile memory or as a protected data stream and is removed or rendered inaccessible after display. Exporting, copying or retransmission of unencrypted artwork is thereby restricted. The workflow comprises importing the digital artwork, validating associated control information, encrypting the artwork before persistent storage, storing the encrypted artwork, authenticating a display request, temporarily decrypting the artwork for rendering, and clearing temporary decrypted data. The system thus reduces the availability of reproducible unencrypted copies and prevents or limits unauthorised diffusion of the digital artwork.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

The encrypted digital art files are stored in a storage medium for subsequent playback. During playback, the authorized display device, or an associated processing system, derives or retrieves a corresponding decryption key using the unique device identifier and decrypts the digital art files for presentation. Binding the encrypted files to the authorized display device restricts unauthorized access, copying, and playback of the digital artwork.
